name: FUSAR-Ship / FUSAR-Ship1.0
review_basis: Read primary full paper Sections 2–5, Tables 2/4/5, Figure 15, supplement Table S1, and current journal release/use guide. Findings are author-reported unless explicitly described as arithmetic or document comparison.
sample_unit: A 512×512 amplitude chip labelled by its central marine object; chip, ship identity and parent scene are different units.
collection_method: The authors processed 126 Gaofen-3 scenes using sea/land separation, candidate extraction and SAR/AIS matching. This selects observations through an annotation pipeline rather than an exhaustive census.
label_generation: AIS and associated vessel-type information supply ship labels; difficult dense nearshore matches require manual correction. Section 5 admits residual category errors and chips containing several ship types but labelled only by the central ship.
negative_policy: Six explicitly constructed non-ship categories include strong false alarms, bridges/coastlines, coastal land/islands, wave clutter, ordinary sea and land.
partition_evidence: Section 5 reports a random 70/30 division and four randomly selected scene demonstrations; it does not establish a parent-scene or vessel-disjoint test.
quality_control: Authors describe manual correction and consistent crop/box conventions, but acknowledge registration errors. Independent label-accuracy measurement was not performed here.
evaluation_meaning: The reported preliminary experiment groups samples into eight categories, including false alarms; it is not evaluation across every node of the 15/98-category hierarchy.
independence_limits: Multiple observations can share scenes, vessels and background. Four demonstration scenes are not documented as independent of the chip pool.
new_findings: Primary Section 4.2 says 10,125 chips; Figure 15 and the current portal say 16,144. Table 2 also contains the smaller experimental population. No explicit version mapping reconciles them.
Central-object-only labels and AIS mismatches are acknowledged by the authors, not merely hypothetical audit concerns.
interpretation: The release combines informative AIS-linked labels with documented selection and label ambiguity. Current portal totals should remain release-specific; the smaller paper population must not be silently substituted.
unresolved: Relationship between the 10,125-chip paper population and 16,144-chip release.
Per-class correction/error rates; vessel- and scene-disjoint partitions.

name: HRSID
review_basis: Read official README and commit histories; independently parsed the single checked-in COCO annotation JSON in memory. No imagery/archive downloaded. Original paper full text was unavailable from IEEE; paper-release claims remain distinct.
sample_unit: An 800×800 image tile with ship polygons/boxes; repository filenames also encode apparent parent-scene identifiers and crop windows.
collection_method: The README describes varied high-resolution SAR sources. The inspected JSON contains 136 distinct filename prefixes, consistent with multiple tiles per source; prefix interpretation is metadata evidence, not verified geolocation.
label_generation: Independently checked schema includes image_id, category_id/name, polygon segmentation, area, bbox and iscrowd; every listed category is ship.
negative_policy: The inspected file has 215 image records without annotations. These are annotation-empty records, not independently confirmed ship-free scenes. The README separately offers 400 background images.
partition_evidence: The file named train2017.json contains 3,573 images and 9,870 annotations. Its only recorded upload is 24 November 2019, preceding 2020 README/download updates. It is not the published 3,642-image derivative training partition.
quality_control: Checks found unique annotation IDs, positive box dimensions and iscrowd=0 throughout. These structural checks do not establish polygon accuracy, label completeness or image validity.
evaluation_meaning: Detection and segmentation assess different geometry. The published 5,604/16,951 release totals cannot be validated by treating this older training file as the complete dataset.
independence_limits: Only one annotation partition is checked into this repository. Cross-split parent-scene overlap cannot be tested; 136 prefixes within training do not prove leakage.
new_findings: The old checked-in annotation file and linked release are materially different documented artifacts.
215 annotation-empty records qualify any blanket claim that the repository contains only positive tiles.
The 16,951 versus SARDet's 16,969 instance difference remains unresolved; the older JSON does not explain it.
interpretation: HRSID documentation supports a useful distinction between published dataset totals, linked packages and an older repository artifact. Structural validity should not be described as a full annotation-quality audit.
unresolved: Exact correspondence between old JSON and current download packages.
Original annotation adjudication and source-scene partition rules.

name: MSTAR
review_basis: Read official archive overview, public targets, clutter, T-72 variants, mixed targets and conversion-tool descriptions; reread SAMPLE Sections 1/2.1/2.3 for documented use of original collection records.
sample_unit: Depending on subcollection, an aspect-dependent target chip, a replicate physical target, or a full clutter scene. There is no verified unified chip denominator.
collection_method: Official pages describe separate 1995/1996 collections, multiple scenes and STARLOS/Sandia acquisition conditions. The variant and mixed-target collections span a broader condition set than the initial public-target page.
label_generation: Known collection targets and replicate identities provide labels; SAMPLE describes historical photographs, configuration notes and image-header metadata. This is curated collection truth, not evidence of independently adjudicated labels in every redistributed chip package.
negative_policy: The official archive includes 100 separate rural/urban clutter scenes. Their existence does not establish that a particular ten-class classification subset includes negatives or exhaustive detection annotations.
partition_evidence: Official sections group data by collection, scene and acquisition condition; they do not define one universal train/test partition. A paper's subset protocol cannot be substituted for archive-level documentation.
quality_control: Collection provenance and known target configurations are documented. Archive-wide duplicate, missing-file and label-error checks were not performed.
evaluation_meaning: Closed-label chip classification measures discrimination among selected historical exemplars. It does not by itself measure background rejection, unseen-identity recognition or full-scene detection.
independence_limits: Different views can share the same physical target, scene and conditions. SAMPLE explicitly notes shared operating conditions as a limitation of MSTAR-derived evaluations.
new_findings: Variant/mixed-target pages directly demonstrate collection and scene heterogeneity omitted by a single ten-class summary.
SLICY is a known engineering reflector target, not an additional ordinary vehicle class.
The program name alone does not establish motion tracks or temporal ground truth.
interpretation: MSTAR should be described as an archive family with protocol-dependent subsets. Reporting target-type, physical-exemplar and image counts separately is necessary to interpret published results.
unresolved: Complete manifest and annotation completeness for each public subcollection.
Which replicate identities and source scenes overlap within any specific published split.

name: OpenSARShip (original release)
review_basis: Read original and 2.0 author abstracts through OpenAlex indexing, current SJTU project/detail/download pages, FUSAR's comparison paragraph and the secondary EasySAR reader README. Original full methods text was not recovered.
sample_unit: Original paper: 11,346 SAR ship chips associated with AIS. This does not count unique vessels, parent scenes or negative backgrounds.
collection_method: Original abstract establishes Sentinel-1/AIS integration. FUSAR's later comparison reports 41 Sentinel-1 scenes, five Asian ports and concentrated ship-type populations; these details are secondary, not independently reconstructed.
label_generation: AIS-associated information supplies reported type/metadata. Original matching, manual review and exclusion procedures remain unverified. The later 2.0 abstract explicitly adds interference labels and type levels.
negative_policy: An interference-labelled chip is not necessarily a ship-free negative. Neither accessible abstract provides a count or exhaustive policy for empty/background scenes.
partition_evidence: No authoritative original split manifest was inspected. Image count alone cannot establish vessel-, acquisition- or port-disjoint evaluation.
quality_control: Author claims of reliability were not reproduced. The EasySAR tool README identifies Ship.xml, Metedata.xml and several patch representations, but is secondary documentation rather than the original schema specification.
evaluation_meaning: The original paper describes ship interpretation and imagery-quality assessment. The 2.0 abstract illustrates geometric-parameter extraction. These are different questions from open-scene detection with measured false alarms.
independence_limits: Repeated acquisitions and alternative patch representations can inflate apparent sample diversity; exact identity linkage and duplication could not be checked.
new_findings: SJTU currently reports 34,528 chips; the 2.0 author abstract reports exactly 34,528. This resolves the count as an expanded version, not a correction to original 11,346.
Version 2.0 explicitly adds interference labelling and type levels, so its labels cannot be assumed identical to the original.
Download suffixes _1/_2 are not proven publication-version identifiers.
interpretation: Original and expanded releases require separate catalogue identities. Current portal text is insufficient to infer the original matching quality or evaluation partitions.
unresolved: Original full annotation/matching method and exact XML semantics.
Per-version negative policy, unique-vessel counts and partition independence.

name: SAMPLE
review_basis: Reread manuscript Sections 2/4.1, Tables 1/4/5 and public verify.py; independently counted MAT paths in original data-addition and current Git trees. No image arrays inspected.
sample_unit: A measured observation and matched simulated counterpart. Alternative MAT/PNG representations and paired domains are not independent physical exemplars.
collection_method: Authors restrict selection to ten vehicle/serial combinations with satisfactory historical CAD models and compatible collection records. Models were manually compared with photographs/notes; simulation backgrounds were not matched to measured ground planes.
label_generation: Known vehicle identity and measured-source metadata determine class/pair labels. Per-pair registration changes measured-image alignment; filename fields permit correspondence without reading arrays.
negative_policy: The public release consists of labelled target chips. Background pixels within a chip are not an independently labelled clutter-only negative set.
partition_evidence: Paper protocols hold out an acquisition condition, but the same small set of physical exemplars remains represented. This is not evidence of an unseen-vehicle-identity partition.
quality_control: Authors report repeated manual CAD checking. verify.py checks file families, metadata keys and permitted condition ranges, and can rewrite MAT metadata; its presence is not proof an untouched archive passed a read-only audit.
evaluation_meaning: Comparisons concern a narrow paired measured/simulated domain and closed class list. Better matching does not establish physical fidelity for unrepresented configurations or environments.
independence_limits: Many views share one serial per category; synthetic and measured members share intended geometry. Registration and repeated representations create additional dependencies.
new_findings: The first data-addition commit, dated 27 September 2019, already has 1,345 measured and 1,345 synthetic MAT paths.
Later listed commits modify README only. Thus later repository deletion does not explain the manuscript's 1,366-pair Table 5; discrepancy predates public upload.
Paper explicitly distinguishes matched targets from unmatched ground/background.
interpretation: The history narrows, but does not solve, the count mismatch. Report manuscript and public-manifest denominators separately, without inventing missing samples or treating one pair as two independent examples.
unresolved: Why manuscript Table 5 exceeds both public Git trees by 21 pairs.
Image-level corruption, exact alignment residuals and release-specific metadata completeness.

name: SAR-AIRcraft-1.0
review_basis: Retrieved primary full HTML through the journal page's own read endpoint; read Sections 2.1/2.2,4.1–4.3 and Tables 1/3. No dataset package or model code executed.
sample_unit: Detection images contain multiple aircraft; recognition examples are separate crops extracted using the labelled boxes. Neither is a unique-airframe count.
collection_method: Section 2.1 specifies 1 m, single-polarization Gaofen-3 spotlight imagery selected primarily from three named civil airports across multiple times, with four image sizes.
label_generation: Section 2.2 explicitly describes horizontal Pascal VOC XML boxes: image size, aircraft name and xmin/ymin/xmax/ymax. This resolves the previous schema uncertainty; the described release schema is not a scattering-keypoint annotation specification.
negative_policy: The paper describes background facilities and false detections but does not enumerate aircraft-free images or an exhaustive negative-selection rule.
partition_evidence: Section 2.2 reports 7:1:2 training/validation/test image division. Section 4.2 separately reports 13,513/2,950 cropped-instance recognition partitions. The previous object-count table must not stand in for image split counts.
quality_control: The source describes representation and labelled examples, but gives no verified annotator agreement/error rate in reviewed sections. No independent label checks were performed.
evaluation_meaning: Detection, crop recognition accuracy and joint type-plus-localization evaluation are distinct. Recognition results assume ground-truth cropping; they do not include the preceding localization failure rate.
independence_limits: The paper reports multiple times/viewpoints, primarily at three named airports, but does not establish airport-, date- or airframe-disjoint splitting.
new_findings: Full methods resolve primary sensor/mode, civil-airport scope, XML schema and validation-split existence.
Table 3 belongs specifically to box-cropped recognition, explaining why its units differ from the 7:1:2 image protocol.
Other denotes aircraft outside the six named classes, not a background class.
interpretation: This is a geographically concentrated civil-type image benchmark with separate evaluation units. Published crop recognition and detection scores cannot be interpreted as one interchangeable measure.
unresolved: Exact image manifests and assignment by airport/date/parent acquisition.
Annotator process, uncertain-type handling and aircraft-free image counts.

name: SARDet-100K
review_basis: Read paper Tables 1/2 and Appendix A.2, official README, dataset parser SAR_Det.py and base SARDet_100k configuration. Code was inspected statically, not run.
sample_unit: A standardized source image or overlapping patch, plus repeated image-local object annotations; not necessarily an independent scene or unique object.
collection_method: Ten existing datasets are assembled. Larger images from three sources are cropped with overlap; existing partitions are retained where available, otherwise image partitions are created.
label_generation: Annotation formats are converted to COCO and broad categories reconciled. The described standardization is not a documented reannotation of every image for every category.
negative_policy: The inspected base training configuration enables empty-ground-truth filtering. The parser preserves test-mode image records; therefore raw image totals do not automatically equal the images admitted during training.
partition_evidence: Paper reports three partitions. Final base-config assignments reference separate val.json and test.json, although README still contradicts itself about test-download availability. Configuration paths do not prove those files are publicly downloadable.
quality_control: Parser asserts unique annotation IDs and excludes ignored, nonintersecting, nonpositive-area/tiny or out-of-category annotations. Structural filtering is not verification of class correctness or exhaustive labels.
evaluation_meaning: The inspected configuration uses COCO bounding-box metrics, including classwise test output. Optional mask fields in the parser do not make those reported results segmentation evaluations.
independence_limits: Overlap can repeat one object across patches; aggregate data also overlap constituent benchmarks. Source-scene leakage and cross-category annotation completeness were not independently tested.
new_findings: Static code establishes negative-image and invalid-annotation handling beyond the paper's headline counts.
The final test configuration is distinct from validation; an earlier alias is overwritten and should not be misread as the final setting.
Current parser/config provide no explanation for the HRSID 18-instance or SSDD 131-instance count differences.
interpretation: The benchmark standardizes representation and reporting, while inheriting heterogeneous annotation and sampling assumptions. Its size is a patch/annotation denominator, not a new independent acquisition population.
unresolved: Public test-package status and source-to-derived annotation provenance.
Deduplication, parent-scene partitioning and complete six-category coverage per image.

name: SSDD / Official SSDD
review_basis: Read primary 2021 paper Sections 1.4,3.1–3.3,4,6.1–6.3, Table 6/7 and test-set descriptions; compared SARDet's derivative statistics. No archive annotation files inspected.
sample_unit: An image with ship instances; box, rotated-box and polygon labels represent different geometry for those instances, not three independent observations.
collection_method: The official release revisits heterogeneous multi-sensor imagery and corrects the initial annotation version. It is not described as a fresh independent sensor campaign.
label_generation: The paper describes drawing polygons with LabelMe and deriving horizontal and minimum-area rotated boxes from polygon outlines. This establishes the documented geometric relationship; released annotation variants were not compared file by file. The paper describes three stored image channels repeating one grayscale channel, not three radar measurements.
negative_policy: Polygon masks define background outside ships. That does not establish an enumerated, independently verified ship-free image subset; no such count was found in reviewed sections.
partition_evidence: Table 6 fixes 928 training and 232 test images using final filename digits; no unique validation set is supplied. The 232 test images comprise 46 inshore and 186 offshore images.
quality_control: Authors identify and correct missing/false labels and loose boxes. They do not report an independently reproduced post-correction error rate here.
evaluation_meaning: Inshore means the image contains land, not proof a particular ship is moored. Section 6.3 defines size using label-type-specific pixel-area thresholds; this is not a uniform physical vessel-size classification.
independence_limits: A deterministic filename split improves repeatability but does not establish parent-scene, acquisition-date or vessel independence. Derived annotation types are correlated.
new_findings: Primary full text resolves exact official split and confirms absent unique validation set.
Inshore/offshore is image-context labelling; size definitions vary between box, rotated-box and polygon tasks.
Original 2,456 versus SARDet 2,587 remains unresolved: paper discusses corrections, but the reviewed text does not provide a 131-instance reconciliation ledger.
interpretation: Version, geometric annotation task and partition must accompany reported numbers. Three-channel storage, multiple label types and repeated crops should not be counted as added sensor diversity or independent data.
unresolved: Exact corrected object inventory and provenance of the 131-instance difference.
Negative-only inventory, annotator agreement and acquisition-disjoint split evidence.

name: DIOR
review_basis: Independently read the original paper's dataset and evaluation sections and compared its totals with the current creator page. Collection and annotation procedures below are author-reported; no image archive or annotation sample was audited.
sample_unit: 23,463 RGB images, each 800×800 pixels, containing multiple objects. The original paper reports 192,472 instances; the current creator page reports 192,518.
collection_method: Earth-observation interpretation experts selected Google Earth imagery from more than 80 countries, deliberately varying weather, season, quality, scale and appearance. Reported spatial resolution is 0.5–30 m. This is curated coverage, not probability sampling of geography.
label_generation: Annotators manually drew horizontal boxes with LabelMe for 20 broad categories. Class selection combined categories shared by earlier benchmarks with literature and application considerations. Ships and vehicles dominate instance counts; the ontology mixes objects and larger facilities.
negative_policy: The reviewed construction section does not establish a separately enumerated negative-only image set or an exhaustive background sampling rule. Unannotated pixels should not be treated as independently verified absence of every object type.
partition_evidence: The paper reports random image-level splits: 5,862 training, 5,863 validation and 11,738 test images. Train plus validation is 11,725. The stated goal is similar distributions; no location, capture-date or physical-object holdout is established.
quality_control: Expert collection and manual annotation are documented. The reviewed sections do not specify an independent second-pass audit, inter-annotator agreement or measured annotation-error rate.
evaluation_meaning: Paper AP/mAP evaluates class-labelled horizontal detections with more than 50% box overlap. It measures the chosen categories and geometry, not fine aircraft/ship subtype recognition.
independence_limits: Multiple categories can coexist in one image, so per-category image counts cannot be added into unique-image totals. Google Earth source-scene overlap and repeated observations were not audited.
new_findings: Recovered exact original split counts.
Identified the 46-instance difference between original-paper and current-page totals.
interpretation: DIOR is a broad detection benchmark with deliberately diverse imagery. Its published scale is credible as an author-reported release description; geographic diversity alone does not establish independent evaluation.
unresolved: Release manifest explaining the instance-count change.
Negative-only coverage and location-level split correspondence.

name: DIOR-R
review_basis: Independently read the AOPG paper's DIOR-R description and compared it with the creator page and original DIOR paper. This is a documentation review, not verification of released files.
sample_unit: The same 23,463 images used by DIOR, with oriented annotations. AOPG's dataset paragraph reports 192,518 instances, while its introduction reports 192,512; original DIOR reported 192,472.
collection_method: The paper explicitly reuses DIOR imagery rather than describing a newly acquired image collection. Its Google Earth provenance and deliberately varied scenes therefore derive from DIOR; oriented relabelling does not add independent scenes.
label_generation: Authors say they annotate oriented bounding boxes for every instance across the same 20 broad classes. The inspected DIOR-R paragraph does not provide an annotator workforce, calibration procedure, adjudication rule or detailed difficult-object policy.
negative_policy: No separate negative-image collection or revised background-coverage rule is established. Existing DIOR image content is inherited, but identical object inclusion cannot be assumed given the conflicting instance totals.
partition_evidence: AOPG reports using the trainval set for training and the test set for evaluation. The paper establishes image reuse; an independently checked mapping of DIOR-R release filenames to DIOR's original splits was not obtained.
quality_control: The existence and intended oriented geometry are confirmed by both paper and creator documentation. Neither establishes a measured annotation error rate. Added orientation is not itself evidence of improved category correctness.
evaluation_meaning: The benchmark tests oriented object localisation and broad-category classification. Horizontal DIOR results and oriented DIOR-R results have different geometric matching conditions and are not interchangeable measurements.
independence_limits: DIOR and DIOR-R substantially share observations by construction. They must not be counted as independent image corpora, nor does an image-level split prove location or object identity separation.
new_findings: The primary paper itself contains two DIOR-R totals, 192,512 and 192,518.
The exact same-image relationship is explicit in the dataset paragraph.
interpretation: Treat DIOR-R as an annotation variant with useful orientation information and inherited sampling limitations. Attach the exact release and annotation task to any reported result.
unresolved: Canonical instance count and released split mapping.
Oriented-box checking process and ambiguous-object conventions.

name: DOTA v1.0
review_basis: Independently checked current creator documentation and the later comprehensive DOTA paper, whose version tables identify v1.0. Annotation procedures are the authors' retrospective account, not an external audit of the 2018 archive.
sample_unit: 2,806 variable-sized images with 188,282 annotated instances in 15 classes. Original source images are the counting unit; downstream tiles are additional representations of those images.
collection_method: The later source table assigns the shared v1.0/v1.5 images to 2,375 Google Earth and 431 GF/JL images. It gives no aerial/CycloMedia images for this set; the current generic source list should not be applied retroactively.
label_generation: Oriented quadrilaterals carry category and difficult flags. The common pipeline uses expert examples to train volunteers; initial labels from the plain group are checked by senior volunteers and authors. Failed images return for correction.
negative_policy: The paper describes Google Earth collection as foreground-rich. It acknowledges tiny missed objects and subsequently adds sub-10-pixel instances in v1.5. Thus unlabelled small objects in v1.0 are not necessarily true negatives.
partition_evidence: Authors and creator page report approximately one-half training, one-sixth validation and one-third test. Version tables give 98,990, 28,853 and 60,439 instances, respectively. Geographic, temporal and physical-object disjointness is not established by these proportions.
quality_control: Repeated review is documented, but the statement that missed objects are negligible is an author claim without an independent error estimate in the inspected material.
evaluation_meaning: Horizontal-box and oriented-box detection are separate tasks. The comprehensive paper specifies VOC2007 mAP; quadrilateral overlap changes the localisation criterion. Generic plane and ship labels do not encode fine subtypes.
independence_limits: v1.5 reuses these images and v2.0 contains earlier material. Version totals cannot be summed as independent scenes. Tiling may create correlated observations; the archive was not audited for duplicates.
new_findings: Corrected the earlier attribution of CycloMedia imagery to v1.0.
Established that later tiny-object coverage changes the meaning of unlabelled background.
interpretation: Use v1.0 as a historically specific annotation release. Its count, geometry and coverage policy must travel together when interpreting benchmark results.
unresolved: Exact source-scene and split overlap.
Version-specific annotation omissions and archive fidelity.

name: DOTA v1.5
review_basis: Independently compared the comprehensive DOTA paper's version tables with the current official page. This establishes a documentation discrepancy; no archive-level recount was performed.
sample_unit: The same 2,806 images and image partitions as v1.0, with denser labels and 16 categories. The current site reports 403,318 instances; the inspected paper's Table V reports 402,089.
collection_method: No new image acquisition is claimed for v1.5. The comprehensive paper attributes these images to Google Earth and GF/JL satellites, with zero aerial/CycloMedia images in its source table.
label_generation: The release adds extremely small instances, described as less than 10 pixels, and the container-crane category. It retains oriented quadrilateral annotations. The paper's common workflow uses expert examples, trained volunteers, senior checking and author review.
negative_policy: Small objects omitted in v1.0 can become positives in v1.5. This directly changes annotation completeness and evaluation background; the increase in object totals should not be interpreted as more independent imagery.
partition_evidence: The authors explicitly preserve v1.0 image splits. The paper gives 210,631 training, 69,565 validation and 121,893 test instances, summing to its 402,089 total, not the current site's total.
quality_control: The review workflow is documented but no independent measured residual-error rate is supplied. Version-table consistency can be checked arithmetically; it cannot resolve what the current downloadable archive contains.
evaluation_meaning: Detection remains broad-category classification plus horizontal or oriented localisation under the specified task. Added tiny objects and a new class change the denominator and difficulty of reported results.
independence_limits: This is a reannotation of v1.0 observations. Cross-version comparisons must account for label coverage and taxonomy changes, and separate versions cannot serve as independent source evidence.
new_findings: Table V resolves the paper's 402,089 as an overall total; its container-crane row is 237.
Current official total differs by 1,229 instances, with no inspected change log resolving it.
interpretation: Preserve both cited totals with their versions rather than silently choosing one. v1.5 primarily deepens annotation coverage and cannot be counted as a new image collection.
unresolved: Manifest or correction explaining 402,089 versus 403,318.
Location-level and date-level partition independence.

name: DOTA v2.0
review_basis: Independently read construction, source, version and evaluation sections of the comprehensive paper and checked official counts. Collection quality and residual annotation accuracy remain author-reported.
sample_unit: 11,268 source images containing 1,793,658 instances in 18 categories, including airport and helipad. Counts include earlier-version material and additional images, not an entirely independent second corpus.
collection_method: Table III separates 10,186 Google Earth, 516 GF/JL and 566 aerial images. Google Earth selection is foreground-rich, while larger satellite/aerial images contribute more background. GF/JL panchromatic imagery is converted from 10-bit to 8-bit.
label_generation: Experts supply examples; trained volunteers create quadrilateral labels; senior volunteers and authors check them and return failures. Plane nose, wingtips and tail guide boxes; corner order encodes heading where discernible. Ambiguous direction and tiny objects remain annotation challenges.
negative_policy: More low-foreground imagery broadens background coverage, but the paper does not establish that all unannotated content is negative. Missed tiny objects are acknowledged, and difficult flags are part of the format.
partition_evidence: Official splits are 1,830 training, 593 validation, 2,792 test-dev and 6,053 test-challenge images, with 268,627, 81,048, 353,346 and 1,090,637 instances. These independently sum to the headline totals.
quality_control: The review process is documented; a negligible miss proportion is an author assessment, not an independently verified error rate. GSD is available for only about 30% of images; acquisition dates are incomplete and geolocations are not released.
evaluation_meaning: The paper uses separate horizontal and oriented tasks with VOC2007 mAP and evaluates on test-dev. Hidden labels reduce direct test-label access but do not demonstrate geographic independence.
independence_limits: Mixed sensors, incomplete GSD/date metadata and inherited images limit claims about independent distribution coverage. The much larger test portion is a benchmark design choice, not a representative geographic sample.
new_findings: Source counts distinguish the aerial imagery introduced beyond the earlier versions.
Paper-era test-image access wording differs from current challenge-specific availability.
interpretation: A large, well-documented broad-object benchmark whose source mixture and incomplete metadata should accompany aggregate performance claims.
unresolved: Source-scene overlap across partitions.
Current test-challenge availability and version-specific access conditions.

name: FAIR1M (original paper release)
review_basis: Independently read the original paper's construction, annotation and benchmark sections. The record is tied to that release; later challenge packages were not treated as identical.
sample_unit: 15,266 images and approximately 1.02 million annotated instances, organized into 37 fine categories under five broad groups. This is an image-and-instance detection collection, not a set of independent object identities.
collection_method: Authors collected Google Earth and Gaofen imagery at 0.3–0.8 m resolution over more than 100 airports, harbours and cities. Gaofen preprocessing includes cloud/noise rejection, block adjustment, orthorectification, pansharpening and hue adjustment.
label_generation: Ordered oriented boxes encode class and direction, with occlusion or uncertain-direction information. The ontology combines named civil aircraft models with functional ship/vehicle classes, courts and roads. Other-airplane, other-ship and other-vehicle absorb unlisted types.
negative_policy: The paper states a 16-pixel annotation threshold, but its example says ships longer than 13 m need not be labelled at 0.8 m resolution. That example is internally difficult to reconcile; no corrected rule was established. Small unlabelled objects cannot automatically be treated as verified negatives.
partition_evidence: The original paper reports training/validation/test proportions of one-half, one-sixth and one-third, with test labels withheld for server evaluation. It does not establish geographic or date-disjoint selection in the inspected split description.
quality_control: Authors describe paired independent reannotation and merging, supervisor checks of location/category/orientation, and expert inspection. No external error-rate or agreement audit was performed here.
evaluation_meaning: Besides ordinary AP, the paper introduces FIoU and confidence-sensitive fine-grained mAP_F, with a 0.5 FIoU threshold. These are distinct from plain IoU-based mAP and require their metric name.
independence_limits: Multitemporal and multisource imagery can cover the same region. Preprocessing alignment and broad geographic coverage do not demonstrate independent partitions.
new_findings: Recovered original split proportions and the distinct mAP_F definition.
Identified contradictory wording in the size-threshold example.
interpretation: Its detailed taxonomy and review procedure are documented strengths of construction, while mixed category granularity and metric differences limit simple cross-dataset comparisons.
unresolved: Corrected annotation-size rule.
Release-specific file counts, geographic split independence and dataset licence.

name: FGSC-23
review_basis: Independently retrieved and read the publisher's full PDF, extending the earlier abstract-only review. Construction and experiment details below are author-reported; neither the chip archive nor individual labels were inspected.
sample_unit: 4,052 object-centred image chips across 23 categories: 22 ship categories and one ship-like non-ship category. The paper reports class imbalance, with class 11 containing only 27 examples.
collection_method: Sources are Google Earth and GF-2 panchromatic imagery at 0.4–2 m resolution; approximately 1,600 chips explicitly derive from HRSC2016. Crops align the object centre with the image centre and include panchromatic and composite-colour appearances.
label_generation: Humans assign chip categories plus integer aspect ratio in the range 1–13 and axis angle from 0–180 degrees. Attributes are encoded in filenames. This angle represents undirected axial orientation, not a complete directed bow heading.
negative_policy: The negative category contains non-ship objects resembling ships. It provides a specific confusion class, not evidence of systematic sampling across all background conditions or full-scene false-positive behaviour.
partition_evidence: The experiment randomly selects 20% within each category for testing, except class 11, where 10 examples are test and 17 training. The paper describes augmentation of the training subset after this split. Source-image or physical-ship grouping is not established.
quality_control: The paper documents human labels and attribute conventions, but the reviewed construction section does not describe independent adjudication, agreement statistics or a measured error rate.
evaluation_meaning: Per-class accuracy, overall accuracy and confusion matrices evaluate classification of centred chips. Overall accuracy reflects the imbalanced class frequencies. The special small-class split makes a blanket 80/20 description incomplete.
independence_limits: HRSC2016 reuse is explicitly documented. Multiple chips may share source imagery or vessel identity; a random chip split does not resolve this relationship.
new_findings: Established approximately 1,600-chip HRSC2016 dependency.
Recovered the smallest-class split exception, filename attributes and non-profit academic-use restriction.
interpretation: FGSC-23 has more verifiable methodological detail than its abstract alone conveyed. Its negative category and shape attributes should be interpreted within a cropped classification task.
unresolved: Source-chip manifest and duplicate/identity correspondence.
Complete label-name mapping and independent annotation audit.

name: FGSD
review_basis: Independently read the original full paper's collection, hierarchy, annotation and baseline sections. Numerical totals and conventions are primary-source reports; no public archive or individual label was audited.
sample_unit: 2,612 selected labelled images, each 930×930 pixels, drawn from 4,736 collected pictures. The paper counts 5,634 ships and separately 1,366 docks; neither number is the image count.
collection_method: Authors used current and historical Google Earth imagery from 17 ports in four countries, reporting 0.12–1.93 m resolution. They shifted and rotated map views while collecting samples and retained port ID, resolution and Google Earth layer information.
label_generation: There are 43 ship types plus a separate dock class, with a multilevel ship hierarchy. Both horizontal and rotated boxes are supplied. Heading uses a centre-to-bow vector represented through direction signs, rather than treating a box angle alone as full ship heading.
negative_policy: The labelled subset is selected from collected imagery; the paper does not give a negative-only image inventory or explain why every excluded picture was rejected. Dock is an explicitly labelled class, not a synonym for background.
partition_evidence: Training contains 1,917 images/3,964 ships, validation 268/590 and test 427/1,080. These sum to the stated labelled totals. The inspected paper does not establish a randomization algorithm or port/date/physical-ship holdout.
quality_control: The paper defines label geometry and metadata but does not document a staged independent annotation audit or measured error rate. Those omissions should remain unknown rather than be filled from later papers.
evaluation_meaning: Two baseline tasks predict category with horizontal or rotated boxes, reported through AP and mAP. The inspected baseline description does not pin down all matching and averaging settings, so scores require their exact protocol.
independence_limits: Map shifts, rotations and historical observations may create related views of the same place or vessel. This is a plausible dependence mechanism, not a measured duplicate rate. ShipRSImageNet explicitly reuses FGSD.
new_findings: Clarified heading encoding beyond the rotated box.
Separated collected pictures, labelled images, ships and docks.
interpretation: FGSD documents rich label structure but restricted port sampling. Its public paper alone does not verify a current downloadable release or independent test population.
unresolved: Current creator-controlled archive and dataset licence.
Annotation adjudication, negative sampling and split independence.

name: HRSC2016
review_basis: Independently read the original publisher PDF, especially §2 and its partition algorithm. This resolves the original-paper count; it does not establish which later archive produced the frequently repeated 1,070 figure.
sample_unit: The original paper reports 1,061 labelled images with 2,976 ships, plus 610 separate unannotated images. Of labelled images, 70 contain sea-only backgrounds and 991 sea-land backgrounds; both groups contain ships.
collection_method: Google Earth current/historical imagery was collected from six harbours at 0.4–2 m resolution. Images containing ships were saved with random rotation. Harbour, source, date, scale and approximate coordinates were recorded; the authors warn about shifted Google Earth coordinates.
label_generation: Labels form ship/category/type levels. Uncertain leaf types fall back to the second-level category. Horizontal boxes, rotated boxes and V-shaped bow points are described. Pixel-based segmentation masks are supplied only for test images; the sea-separation evaluation uses both ground-truth sea and ship regions.
negative_policy: Collection explicitly selects images if ships are present. Sea-only means background composition, not negative imagery. The 610 unannotated images are not documented as verified ship-free examples.
partition_evidence: Original splits are 436/181/444 images and 1,207/541/1,228 ships for training/validation/test. Algorithm 1 assigns source images using randomized, hierarchy-aware class processing; this is not a harbour, date or vessel-identity holdout.
quality_control: The paper acknowledges difficult subtype recognition and the cost of expert hiring. Its proposed citizen-scientist approach should not be read as proof that every original label received independent expert adjudication.
evaluation_meaning: The paper separates sea-land separation fitness from class/localisation detection evaluation. Sea separation considers sea overlap and retained ship integrity. One-class ship mAP does not measure fine ship-type accuracy.
independence_limits: Small harbour coverage and historical/rotated observations permit correlated images. The authors' 'Unbiasedness' section describes partition construction, not population-representative sampling.
new_findings: Resolved the original labelled total as 1,061, not 1,070.
Recovered exact splits, fallback labels and the separately unannotated collection.
interpretation: HRSC2016 is a multi-task, hierarchical research collection. Release provenance is essential when later literature changes its count or collapses the label hierarchy.
unresolved: Origin of the later 1,070-image count.
Dataset-specific licence and current release-manifest fidelity.

name: MAR20
review_basis: Independently checked the creator's dataset description and publisher record. The journal full-text route was gated, so collection, checking and split procedures could not be established from the accessible primary material.
sample_unit: The creator reports 3,842 images containing 22,341 aircraft instances across 20 types. The distinction between images and objects is explicit; these totals do not enumerate unique physical aircraft.
collection_method: Accessible documentation identifies a remote-sensing aircraft-recognition dataset but does not provide a verified complete sensor, imagery-provider, geographic or acquisition-date inventory. Sources from other datasets hosted on the same creator page must not be transferred to MAR20.
label_generation: The creator explicitly states that instances have both horizontal and oriented bounding boxes. It does not specify, in that description, an annotator workforce, disagreement handling, unknown-type convention or object-size threshold.
negative_policy: A negative-only image subset, rules for partly visible objects and minimum annotation size were not established. The presence of boxes does not demonstrate exhaustive annotation of all visible aircraft.
partition_evidence: No exact original split counts or partition construction method were verified. Any later implementation's split should be identified as such rather than described as an audited canonical release.
quality_control: The source supports the existence of dual annotation geometry and the reported totals. It does not substantiate an independent error rate, expert consensus or geographic coverage audit.
evaluation_meaning: The labels concern aircraft type and localisation. Horizontal and oriented detections need distinct geometry-aware interpretation; the accessible evidence does not justify reproducing a specific scoring protocol.
independence_limits: The absence of source-scene, date and object-identity metadata in the inspected description leaves dependence unresolved. Large object counts do not establish independent observations.
new_findings: Separated creator citation year 2022 from journal publication in 2023, volume 27(12), pp.2688–2696.
Confirmed explicit CC BY-NC 4.0 and research-purpose wording on the creator page.
interpretation: MAR20 is a creator-documented detection asset with specific annotation and licence statements, but its deeper methodological evidence remains incomplete.

name: MTARSI (original 2019 deposit)
review_basis: Independently read creator-deposited DataCite metadata and the abstract of a later external quality study indexed by OpenAlex. The original archive and that study's full text were not accessible; detailed error counts were therefore not inferred.
sample_unit: 9,385 single-aircraft chips in 20 categories, described as manually expanded. Each chip contains one complete aircraft; image totals are not counts of independent scenes or physical aircraft.
collection_method: The deposit describes Google Earth imagery from 36 airports. Manual expansion is explicit, but the inspected metadata does not specify a parent-image manifest, exact expansion transformations or independent acquisition dates.
label_generation: Seven interpretation specialists labelled the images. The taxonomy combines specific aircraft types with a broad Boeing class, so category granularity is uneven. No box geometry or adjudication protocol is established by the deposit description.
negative_policy: The one-complete-aircraft rule makes this a positive, object-centred classification set. A documented background or no-aircraft category was not established; chip accuracy therefore does not evaluate scene-wide false positives.
partition_evidence: The original canonical split and any grouping of expanded siblings were not verified. The later study's reported validation results are its experimental evidence, not documentation of a universally fixed dataset split.
quality_control: Specialist annotation is author-reported. Gao et al.'s independent study reports labelling errors and limited complexity/heterogeneity, alongside weak results on its adopted external samples despite near-perfect internal validation. Only the abstract was inspected, so the scope and sample selection remain limited.
evaluation_meaning: Classification accuracy measures assignment among the chosen chip labels. The external study demonstrates that internal validation can differ from external-sample performance; it does not establish a universal failure rate for every reuse.
independence_limits: Manual expansion, airport-specific backgrounds and cropped views can correlate samples. No duplicate or split audit was performed, and MTARSI 2 explicitly derives from this collection.
new_findings: Preserved the quality study's abstract-only evidence boundary.
Separated specialist labelling claims from external observations about generalization.
interpretation: The deposit is identifiable and licensed CC BY 4.0, but its count should not be interpreted as independent coverage or its chip task as full-scene detection.
unresolved: Original split and augmentation lineage.
Full-text quality-study protocol and verified per-label corrections.

review_basis: Independently checked the creator-deposited DOI metadata. This supports derivation, reclassification and declared rights; it does not substitute for inspection of archive contents or a methodological paper.
sample_unit: Aircraft image chips assigned to 42 reclassified categories. The inspected deposit description does not give a verified total image count, so the original MTARSI total of 9,385 is not transferred.
collection_method: Richard Rudd-Orthner and Lyudmila Mihaylova's 2021 University of Sheffield deposit explicitly derives from the original MTARSI and adds augmentation. It is not documented as a newly acquired independent set of airports or source scenes.
label_generation: The stated change is reclassification into 42 categories. The metadata does not provide a complete old-to-new label map, explicit unknown/ambiguous cases, annotator qualifications or an independently checked category-error estimate.
negative_policy: No newly introduced no-aircraft/background class or negative-image sampling process is documented. The original's object-centred chip origin remains relevant, but each derivative file was not checked against that rule.
partition_evidence: Training, validation and test counts and the timing of augmentation relative to splitting are not established. Grouping all variants from a parent image within a partition cannot be assumed.
quality_control: The explicit parent DOI is useful provenance evidence. A description of reclassification alone does not show that original label errors were all corrected or independently adjudicated. The deposit acknowledges uneven class frequencies and appearance variation.
evaluation_meaning: A 42-class classification result answers a different label question from the original 20-class task. Changes in category boundaries and augmentation also prevent attributing any score change solely to improved data quality.

interpretation: Treat MTARSI 2 as a traceable reclassified/augmented derivative, with CC BY 4.0 deposit terms. Its methodological gaps remain explicit pending a manifest-level account.

name: MVRSD
review_basis: Independently inspected the creator repository's README and public file listing. These document a claimed dataset and demo, but the demo archive and a full annotation release were not downloaded.
sample_unit: The README reports 3,000 images of 640×640 pixels with 32,626 instances, plus three additional large unlabelled images. The unlabelled images should not be counted as annotated examples or verified negatives.
collection_method: Authors describe Google Earth imagery at 0.3 m resolution from more than 40 military scenarios across Asia, North America and Europe. The term 'scenario' is not defined as an independent scene, location, acquisition or physical-object unit.
label_generation: The repository establishes an object-detection context but the inspected description does not provide a sufficiently complete class ontology, label geometry schema, annotator protocol or treatment of uncertain identities. Specific class detail should not be supplied from the dataset name alone.
negative_policy: Neither a background-only subset nor rules for occlusion, truncation or minimum object size were established. Three unlabelled large images are described as extra material, not a negative class.
partition_evidence: Canonical train/validation/test counts and partition construction are not documented in the inspected README. A geographically broad collection description does not establish geographic separation between partitions.
quality_control: No repeat-labelling process, independent adjudication, measured label-error rate or duplicate analysis is described in the reviewed repository material. The reported counts remain creator claims rather than independently recounted data.
evaluation_meaning: Without a verified ontology, annotation schema and scoring protocol, the dataset's name and headline totals are insufficient to interpret a quantitative benchmark result precisely.
independence_limits: Chip extraction, Google Earth source reuse and the relationship between the additional large images and labelled chips are unresolved. It is not possible to quantify unique scenes from the README.
new_findings: Distinguished the three unlabelled images from the reported annotated set.
Identified that '40 scenarios' is not a documented independence unit.
interpretation: MVRSD has identifiable creator documentation but a shallow publicly verified methodological record. It should remain visibly less substantiated than entries with inspected primary methods.

name: RarePlanes
review_basis: Independently read the primary paper's annotation, real-data and experimental-split sections and checked creator/AWS documentation. Reported quality checks were not independently replicated on image files.
sample_unit: The paper distinguishes 253 real scenes, 112 locations, 14,707 real aircraft and 629,551 synthetic annotations across 50,000 renders. Tiled products and source scenes are different units and must remain separately counted.
collection_method: WorldView-3 scenes cover 22 countries and 2,142 km². Authors stratified large OpenStreetMap aerodromes in the US/Europe by climate, added seven manually chosen locations overlapping earlier datasets, and selected seasonal revisits. Panchromatic, multispectral and pansharpened RGB products have different resolutions.
label_generation: Real aircraft are annotated as ordered nose–wing–tail–wing diamonds, supporting bounding boxes, length and wingspan. Ten visual attributes with 33 choices lead to broad role classes. Synthetic annotations come from simulation, and full instance masks are synthetic-only.
negative_policy: Released 512×512 real tiles overlap by 20% and contain at least one aircraft. Full images are cropped to annotation extents. The positive-tile product is not a random sample of aircraft-free land.
partition_evidence: The paper explicitly allows an airfield in both real training and test sets at different dates and includes at least one scene per country in both. Its synthetic experiment uses 45,000 renders and 5,000 cross-validation renders.
quality_control: A professional service labels the real data and performs its own QC, followed by author QC. This is a reported two-round process; no independent residual-error estimate was calculated here.
evaluation_meaning: Diamond-derived detection geometry and attribute/role recognition differ from exact model identification or real silhouette segmentation. Real and synthetic labels have distinct production processes; combined headline counts do not describe one homogeneous measurement population.
independence_limits: Revisited airfields, overlapping tiles and manually selected overlap locations create explicit dependencies. Synthetic diversity is generated variation, not additional real observations.
new_findings: Confirmed positive-only tile construction and explicit same-airfield split overlap.
Distinguished diamonds from synthetic silhouette masks and scenes from tiles.
interpretation: RarePlanes provides unusually detailed construction metadata, but its documented partitions are not location-disjoint. CC BY-SA 4.0 and public AWS access are verified documentation claims.
unresolved: Archive-level correspondence of tiles, source scenes and releases.
Independent annotation-error estimate.

name: xView (2018 detection dataset)
review_basis: Independently read primary paper sections on collection, annotation, QC and splits and checked official dataset terms. Numerical QC thresholds are author-reported acceptance criteria, not this review's measured label accuracy.
sample_unit: More than one million annotated objects in 60 categories across approximately 1,415 km² of WorldView-3 imagery. The review does not select among conflicting secondary image counts without an official manifest.
collection_method: Authors identify candidate areas from open databases, confirm relevant objects visually, draw areas of interest and extract intersecting 1 km² UTM grid cells. Variation across continents, environments and capture conditions is deliberately sought; sampling is object-conditioned.
label_generation: Workers use a QGIS plugin for horizontal boxes. Each labels a general category, using a child class when confident and falling back to its parent otherwise. Partly visible objects at approximately 20% visibility or less are excluded.
negative_policy: The goal is exhaustive annotation within the selected classes, subject to visibility exclusion. Supervisory checks include empty tiles and incomplete annotation, but no independently verified negative-only distribution is established.
partition_evidence: The public release splits per image, with 59.2%/20.0%/20.8% of objects in train/test/validation and at least five instances per category in each. The paper's separate baseline experiments use a 70/30 split; these protocols must not be conflated.
quality_control: Worker cross-review, supervisor checks and expert gold-standard checks are described. Experts label six 1 km² chips per batch; passing requires precision 0.75 and recall 0.95 at IoU 0.5. Failed batches are remediated, with Tomnod used for difficult chips.
evaluation_meaning: Box-detection AP concerns the chosen mixed object/facility ontology. QC acceptance thresholds do not mean every class or image reaches those values. Parent fallback and merged-object errors affect label interpretation.
independence_limits: Per-image splitting does not establish spatial separation of neighbouring grid cells. Authors acknowledge that tightly packed groups can be mistakenly labelled as one object; buildings and small cars dominate counts.
new_findings: Recovered public split proportions separately from baseline splits.
Established visibility exclusion, parent fallback and gold-standard sampling scope.
interpretation: xView has a substantive documented QC pipeline and CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 data terms, while sampling and split dependencies limit broad generalization claims.
unresolved: Canonical image manifest and location-level partition independence.
Residual class-specific annotation errors.

name: DroneVehicle
review_basis: Full author paper sections III-A–D and V-A3–4 and the official README were inspected. Images and individual annotation files were not audited.
sample_unit: 28,439 RGB/infrared pairs, or 56,878 individual images, with 953,087 modality-specific quadrilateral annotations. Boxes do not count unique physical vehicles.
collection_method: UAV imagery covers roads, residential areas and parking lots by day and night. Distortion correction, affine transformation and cropping align most pairs; exact universal registration is not claimed.
label_generation: Manual labels give four corner coordinates and one of five vehicle classes. The modalities deliberately have different totals because an object may be visible in only one. Four corners describe image geometry, not a segmentation mask or verified physical heading.
negative_policy: No explicit target-free-image sampling rule, exhaustive background annotation policy or ignore-region specification was established in the reviewed sections.
partition_evidence: Published train/validation/test partitions contain 17,990/1,469/8,980 pairs. Corresponding RGB box totals are 286,793/22,462/143,315; infrared totals are 316,411/24,490/159,616.
quality_control: The paper reports removal of poor-quality or blurred images and manual checking of all image data. No independent error-rate or agreement measurement was performed here.

new_findings: Visibility differences explain unequal modality annotation totals; equality is not the published goal.
The README's 840×712 files include a 100-pixel border around a 640×512 image region.

label_generation: DSIAC advertises ground truth, target photographs, meteorology and target/background temperature differences, plus a viewer and user guide. The page does not reveal coordinate conventions, annotation cadence, visibility flags or the exact class ontology.
negative_policy: Neither exhaustive negative coverage nor an explicit absent-target or ignored-object policy is established by the public summary.
partition_evidence: No canonical train/validation/test assignment or evaluation protocol was found on the current page. The later study's selected images cannot supply a full-archive partition.
quality_control: The availability of ground truth and environmental documentation is a publisher claim. No manual, label file, image sample or empirical annotation-quality audit was inspected.
evaluation_meaning: Archive contents support descriptive statements about object imagery and capture metadata. Scores from a paper-specific subset reflect that subset's selection and task, not an official archive-wide benchmark.
independence_limits: Repeated target identities, viewpoints, acquisition runs and shared backgrounds cannot be quantified from the landing page. The historical SENSIAC name was not independently verified as a separate release.
new_findings: The page's 2020 publication and 2026 modification timestamps describe the webpage, not acquisition dates.
Distribution Statement A coexists with DSIAC's stated final-distribution discretion; no request was submitted.
interpretation: A documented military-origin image archive remains substantially opaque at schema level. No scene-narrative, intent or allegiance annotation set is established.

review_basis: The author preprint, published CVPR paper and current TarDAL README were inspected. No image pairs, YOLO label files or split manifests were audited.

independence_limits: Cropped patches are derived observations, not additional independent captures. Source-video, location and object-identity exclusions across experimental selections were not established.
new_findings: Count discrepancies occur within the published paper as well as between paper and README.
The separate 300-pair fusion set must remain distinct from the main detection count.
No separate manually annotated mask product was verified.

label_generation: Sensor signals are warped and subsampled for pixel correspondence. Camera descriptions and recording references accompany the imagery; no formal object-box, mask, track or timed-event annotation schema was established.
negative_policy: No target-free sampling arm or exhaustive object-presence/background policy is defined. Scene content descriptions do not create negative labels.
partition_evidence: No canonical train/validation/test partition was specified in the reviewed article or release metadata. Third-party selected subsets cannot establish the release's original partition.
quality_control: The primary article documents sensor and registration procedures. Versioned release metadata and an explicit CC BY 4.0 license improve traceability, but do not measure residual alignment or annotation accuracy.
evaluation_meaning: Registered multiband inputs are the principal product. The sources do not establish one independent 'correct fused image' or a mandatory benchmark score; subsequent fusion metrics describe their own stated criteria.
independence_limits: The umbrella contains distinct sensor collections, including the separately described TRICLOBS release. Repeated scenes, cameras and frames must not be combined as independent new datasets.
new_findings: The umbrella-versus-individual-dataset distinction prevents combining unrelated counts.
BMP/TIF/MP4 formats are reported across the umbrella, not verified in every subset.
Original v1 is from 2014; v2 is from 2022.
interpretation: This is a multiband imagery resource with acquisition documentation. Military-relevant scene descriptions do not establish a formal military event or identity ontology.

name: TRICLOBS Dynamic Multiband Image Dataset
review_basis: The primary paper, its 16-row scenario table and official release metadata were inspected. Raw BMPs, preview MP4s and accompanying spreadsheets were not downloaded.
sample_unit: Sixteen motion scenarios at three sites occupy 4/4/8 scenario folders. Published frame counts sum to 56,865 multiband frames; this is arithmetic from Table 1, not a file count.
collection_method: Field trials record staged people/vehicle actions with visible, NIR and LWIR sensors. Thermal 384×288 data are interpolated and visible/NIR cropped to common field of view; output is 640×480.
label_generation: Raw sequential 24-bit BMPs encode visible in R, NIR in G and LWIR in B, each eight bits. Table 1 supplies one prose action description per scenario; reference colour photographs and atmospheric/lighting CSV/Excel data provide context.
negative_policy: The scripted recordings have no verified object-detection present/absent schema or dedicated negative population. A prose clip description is not an exhaustive per-frame label.
partition_evidence: No standard learning or evaluation split is specified. The three sites and sixteen scenarios are acquisition organization, not demonstrated independent train/test assignments.
quality_control: The paper explicitly documents unsynchronized channels with maximum timing difference below 9 ms, independent gain-related flicker, vignetting and limited environmental diversity. These are publisher-described limitations, not independently measured defects.
evaluation_meaning: The release supplies registered spectral observations for fusion-related study, without dense boxes, track identities, timed action ranges or an official mandatory task score. Scenario prose describes visible staged activity, not hidden intent.
independence_limits: Many adjacent frames and repeated actions/sites occur within a small set of scripted recordings. Frame counts cannot be interpreted as independent scenarios or independent field trials.
new_findings: MP4s are four-panel visualization previews containing a colour-remapped fusion; the paper says they are not intended for further processing.
Spatial registration does not mean sensor synchronization.
The raw BMP channel packing differs fundamentally from the preview product.
interpretation: TRICLOBS is a qualified exception with genuine clip-level action metadata, while its raw sensor product and presentation previews must remain distinct.
unresolved: Residual spatial/temporal registration measured on files; any annotation products beyond the inspected paper table; independent scene/source grouping.

name: Anti-UAV original / later Anti-UAV300 label
review_basis: Original paper version 3 sections III-A–E, the correction README and the current version table were inspected. Individual videos and label files were not audited.
sample_unit: The original paper reports 318 unaligned RGB/infrared video pairs and about 585,900 box annotations. The later 'Anti-UAV300' label is a release name, not the exact original count.
collection_method: Ground-based paired sensors record mainly DJI/Parrot consumer drones at 25 FPS under varied lighting and backgrounds. Modalities are explicitly unaligned.
label_generation: The coarse stage labels every 25 frames. The paper then describes selecting 30 pairs for detailed per-frame annotation, corrections and 1,000-frame clips. This does not establish independently manual annotation of every released frame or complete interpolation provenance.
negative_policy: An exist flag records presence/absence; an empty prediction represents absence. The paper calls its rectangle field get_rect and describes corner coordinates, which must not be silently equated with later xywh schemas.
partition_evidence: The original train/validation/test allocation is 160/67/91 paired sequences. Training and validation use different clips from the same recordings; the paper describes test recordings as independent.
quality_control: Progressive annotation and manual correction are published claims. The original repository lists four start-frame corrections. Their existence supports version-sensitive review, without establishing a measured residual label-error rate.
evaluation_meaning: State accuracy combines bounding-box IoU on present-target frames with correctly predicted absence, averages within each clip, then across clips. It is neither ordinary classification accuracy nor a metric of event understanding.
independence_limits: Training and validation are not independent at recording level. Cross-version overlap and precise manual/derived label provenance across all release frames remain unaudited.
new_findings: The paper's detailed annotation stage explicitly names 30 selected video pairs.
Seven challenge attributes describe visual/tracking difficulty rather than scenario narratives.
Original field names and coordinate descriptions differ from the later 410 evaluator.
interpretation: The annotation semantics are UAV localization and visible existence. They do not establish military subtype, intent, threat, authorization or allegiance.
unresolved: Frame-level annotation provenance across the entire release; exact version manifests and overlap; independent audit of corrected start frames.

name: Anti-UAV410
review_basis: The dedicated README, loader/evaluator code and GitHub annotation-directory listings were inspected. Publisher full text was unavailable; no video or annotation-file contents were audited.
sample_unit: The README reports 410 infrared videos and over 438,000 manually annotated boxes. Directory listings contain 200/90/120 train/validation/test .txt files; these are metadata counts, not verified video counts.
collection_method: The release describes thermal UAV tracking under varied appearance, clutter, occlusion and out-of-view conditions. Detailed acquisition and paper-level review procedures were not established from accessible materials.
label_generation: The loader finds IR_label.json, checks image/gt_rect count equality and a four-entry initial rectangle. The evaluator interprets rectangles as x,y,width,height. Ten sequence attributes are documented; the README explicitly says frame attributes are incomplete.
negative_policy: Evaluation handles absence: empty or single-value predictions denote absent targets; present frames use box overlap. Some invalid or zero ground-truth cases may be skipped, so file conventions affect the scored population.
partition_evidence: Listed annotation filenames total 410 across the three directories. Train contains 02_6319_0000-1499.txt and test contains 02_6319_1500-2999.txt, suggesting adjacent excerpts of one source recording.
quality_control: Manual annotation is an author claim. Loader assertions check limited structural consistency, not box accuracy, exhaustive negatives or inter-annotator agreement. No empirical label audit was performed.
evaluation_meaning: The code averages sequence state accuracies combining present-frame IoU and absence handling. Its separate overlap/precision report adjusts first-frame boxes and mismatched lengths, making the exact evaluation protocol material to interpretation.
independence_limits: The shared filename stem raises a concrete source-independence question; it does not prove duplicated frames. Actual manifests, recording identities and cross-version overlap were not verified.
new_findings: Metadata establishes 200/90/120 annotation-list counts.
A concrete train/test filename pair suggests adjacent source excerpts.
The loader contains a placeholder download URL although README cloud links exist.
interpretation: The accessible evidence establishes a thermal localization/existence schema and incomplete frame attributes, with stronger schema evidence than acquisition-quality evidence.
unresolved: Source-recording separation; complete frame attributes; full-paper annotation protocol; actual video/label consistency and residual errors.

name: AntiUAV600
review_basis: Paper version 2 sections III-A–C and Appendix A, plus the official version table, were inspected. Actual video, box and attribute files were not audited.
sample_unit: Six hundred thermal sequences contain over 723,000 densely annotated frames. The paper gives approximately 337,000/56,000/330,000 frames in train/validation/test.
collection_method: Thermal recordings are 640×512 at 25 FPS and include target appearance, disappearance and complex backgrounds. A target need not be visible in the first frame.
label_generation: The paper describes dense bounding boxes when a UAV is present and 'Not Exist' labels when absent. It claims seven attributes for all frames; that completeness claim was not verified against released files.
negative_policy: Absence is explicitly represented within sequences. This establishes present/absent evaluation states, but does not by itself establish a separately sampled, exhaustive target-free video population.
partition_evidence: The stated sequence split is 300 train, 50 validation and 250 test. These counts are published assignments, without verified source-recording, site or target-identity exclusion.
quality_control: Dense manual annotation and complete attributes are author statements. The reviewed sections do not provide an independently measured label-error rate or inter-annotator agreement, and no such audit was performed here.
evaluation_meaning: The Acc metric combines present-frame localization overlap and correct absence with an additional missed-presence penalty. Consequently it is not directly interchangeable with original Anti-UAV state accuracy despite related terminology.
independence_limits: Cross-version reuse and source-video relationships were not audited. Anti-UAV300, 410 and 600 therefore cannot be added as disjoint captures or independent benchmark populations.
new_findings: The deeper paper review establishes 300/50/250 sequences and approximate per-partition frame totals.
First-frame presence is not guaranteed.
All-frame attribute completeness is a paper claim, distinct from the 410 README's incompleteness caveat.
interpretation: This release evaluates UAV localization and existence through time, including initial absence. Its labels do not establish scenario narratives, intent or military identity.
unresolved: Actual schema/attribute completeness; source-independent partitions; cross-version overlap; detailed negative-population sampling and label-quality measurements.

review_basis: Primary paper sections III-A–C and evaluation descriptions and the official release README were inspected. Individual images, trajectories and ground-truth files were not audited.
sample_unit: The detection subset has 10,000 images and 10,109 boxes. A separate tracking subset has twenty videos, averaging 1,240 frames. Table object totals must not be read as image counts.
collection_method: Visible-light imagery covers varied outdoor scenes, illumination and weather, with a wide range of image sizes. More than 35 visually represented drone types do not establish 35 annotated classes.
label_generation: The authors claim precise manual detection boxes and per-frame tracking rectangles. The two subsets support distinct detection and initialized tracking evaluations; neither establishes a fine-grained platform ontology.
negative_policy: Section III-C explicitly includes out-of-view among challenges, but the inspected descriptions do not establish an absent-target schema, negative-image sampling policy or absence-scoring rule.

quality_control: Manual precision is an author claim. A second-review protocol, agreement statistic and detailed image-source provenance were not verified; no annotation-error sampling was conducted.
evaluation_meaning: Detection mAP evaluates UAV boxes. Tracking overlap success, centre precision and normalized precision evaluate trajectories under their stated initialization and localization conventions. These metrics do not assess authorization, event semantics or intent.
independence_limits: The image partition counts do not establish source-video or geographic disjointness. Authors' analysis reports concentration of targets near image centres, limiting claims of uniform spatial coverage.
new_findings: The paper names out-of-view difficulty without establishing a corresponding absence schema in the reviewed material.
Visual drone-type diversity is not evidence of a multi-class label set.
Detection and tracking sample counts and metrics must remain separate.
interpretation: The evidence supports generic visible-light UAV localization and trajectories, with documented central-position bias and limited tracking-video count.

name: Military Vehicles in Low-FPS UAV Footage validation benchmark
review_basis: Primary paper sections III-A–C, IV opening, evaluation tables and access statement, plus the linked request form, were inspected. No request was submitted or footage/annotations downloaded.
sample_unit: The benchmark comprises 119 videos, 18,421 frames and 58,897 boxes. The request form states all recordings are 5 FPS; these units do not count unique vehicles across online sources.
collection_method: Authors select online UAV videos containing two or more vehicles and varied viewpoints. This is purposive selection from published footage, not a random population sample or verified independent acquisition campaign.
label_generation: Experts assign boxes, three coarse vehicle classes, persistent within-video track IDs and temporal links. The paper's separate discussion of single-frame training labels must not be substituted for the validation benchmark's temporal annotations.
negative_policy: No exhaustive target-free-clip sampling, occlusion/ignore-region rule or annotation-completeness policy was established in the reviewed sections.
