evaluation_meaning: Reported tracking experiments use detections from a common binary detector. HOTA, MOTA, IDF1, association accuracy and identity switches therefore characterize tracking conditional on that detection stream; they do not validate the three-class ontology or full scene understanding.
independence_limits: Online reposts, related clips and source chains were not independently deduplicated. A persistent ID establishes within-video continuity, not identity across recordings.
new_findings: The common binary detection stream materially conditions the reported tracking scores.
Multi-vehicle clip selection shapes the evaluation population.
The request form restricts use to the declared purpose and requires authorization for redistribution or repurposing.
interpretation: The annotations establish coarse military-vehicle categories, location and within-clip identity. They do not establish exact platforms, allegiance, intent or event narratives.
unresolved: Source-chain duplication and rights; detailed ignore/occlusion policy; canonical partitions; archive-level label and track consistency.

name: VTUAV / DUT-VTUAV
review_basis: Paper sections 3.1–3.3 and official release notices were inspected. Video pairs, sparse boxes, masks and attribute files were not audited.
sample_unit: Five hundred sequences contain 1,664,549 RGB-T pairs. Manual boxes every ten frames total 326,961 across modalities; 24,464 masks occur at 1 FPS in 100 clips.
collection_method: A UAV captures ordinary targets over a year in two cities: 325 daytime and 175 nighttime clips. Native 640×480 thermal imagery is enlarged to 1920×1080 output.
label_generation: One initial-frame alignment transform is applied to each whole video. Boxes are separately annotated by modality. The paper discusses tracker-guided densification, which does not establish dense manual ground truth. Among 430,960 attributes on 301,678 frames, FM/SV/LR/TVS are automatically defined; other attributes are expert-labelled.
negative_policy: Long-term sequences have target out-of-view periods exceeding twenty consecutive frames. This is a tracking-condition definition, not evidence of a separately sampled target-free-video population.
partition_evidence: The 250/250 train/test split contains 207/43 and 176/74 short-/long-term clips respectively. The mask subset has fifty train and fifty test sequences.
quality_control: Published cadence and separate modality annotations clarify provenance. The release corrected three archive parts in April 2022. No independent mask, box or residual-registration audit was performed.
evaluation_meaning: Maximum success rate uses the greater overlap against modality-specific ground truth to accommodate displacement. Maximum precision is likewise benchmark-specific with a twenty-pixel centre criterion. Mask evaluation uses region Jaccard and contour F-score.
independence_limits: Frame pairs, sparse boxes and masks are distinct counts. Source-video, location and target-identity exclusions between partitions were not verified; initial-frame alignment cannot establish perfect later-frame registration.
new_findings: Whole-video registration uses a transform estimated at the initial frame.
Some challenge attributes are automatic rather than human judgements.
Published localization scores explicitly accommodate modality displacement.
interpretation: VTUAV observes ordinary objects from a UAV, unlike datasets observing UAV targets. It supplies localization, masks and challenge labels, not military scenario or intent annotations.
unresolved: Complete dense-label provenance, if released; residual per-frame alignment; source-independent partitions; quality of corrected archive contents.

label_generation: Targets receive manually drawn pixel-level masks. The verified semantic product is generic target/background shape, rather than military identity, activity or physical object type.

independence_limits: The counts and image split do not prove separate source videos, acquisition sessions or backgrounds. A single image may contain multiple annotated target regions.
new_findings: The deeper review clarifies that target-level detection probability and pixel-level false alarms are not interchangeable rates.
The 1,000/1,001 paper-versus-README discrepancy persists.
Collection object names are not a verified multi-class mask ontology.
interpretation: The dataset evaluates generic infrared target extent and localization. Reported overlap or detection scores cannot establish platform identity or scene semantics.

name: NUDT-SIRST
review_basis: The author paper's synthesis, evaluation and experimental-setting sections and official repository description were inspected. Synthetic images, masks and split lists were not audited.
sample_unit: The release describes 1,327 synthetic 256×256 images. Approximately 37% contain multiple targets; image count is not target count or a count of independent real acquisitions.
collection_method: Gaussian point models and collected target templates are combined with real infrared backgrounds. Background classification and predefined plausibility rules constrain combinations; intensity and blur are adjusted during construction.
label_generation: Target masks derive from the construction process. They are known synthetic labels, not empirical human tracing of newly observed real targets. Point, spot and extended forms describe appearance rather than verified platform classes.
negative_policy: No dedicated target-free image arm was specified in the inspected description. Synthetic background pixels provide negatives, without demonstrating the distribution of wholly empty real scenes.
partition_evidence: The experiment uses a 50%/50% image split. Independence of background images, target templates and source material across the two halves was not established.
quality_control: Authors report manually removing visually poor synthesized images. Such visual selection can improve presentation, but construction-known masks and curation do not independently establish physical realism or real-domain representativeness.
evaluation_meaning: IoU measures mask overlap. Published detection probability matches targets using centroid deviation below three pixels. False-alarm rate counts false/unmatched pixels divided by total image pixels, not the proportion of images containing a false alarm.
independence_limits: Shared backgrounds or target templates may connect nominally separate images; this was not audited. Multiple synthetic examples do not necessarily add independent natural target observations.
new_findings: Background classification, plausibility rules and manual rejection are explicit parts of construction.
Approximately 37% of images are multi-target.
The centroid-based detection metric and pixel-based false-alarm metric use different units.
interpretation: The release is a synthetic generic-target segmentation benchmark with construction-derived masks. Known labels do not establish military identity or observed event ground truth.
unresolved: Background/template separation across partitions; exact split manifests; dedicated negatives; empirical realism and independent label/scene audits.

name: SIRST (often called NUAA-SIRST in later papers)
review_basis: The original WACV paper sections 3.1–3.4 and official README were inspected. Images, masks, boxes and source/partition manifests were not audited.
sample_unit: The original release contains 427 representative images and 480 target instances. One selected image per source sequence is the stated design; SIRST v2 is a separate release.
collection_method: Images are selected from infrared sequences spanning several spectral bands and backgrounds. Each target is confirmed by motion in its source video to distinguish real targets from pulse noise, while evaluation retains a single frame.
label_generation: The paper describes five annotation forms: category, instance segmentation, bounding box, semantic mask and instance spotting. The current README explicitly confirms boxes and semantic masks and says the rest will come; paper scope and confirmed release documentation differ.
negative_policy: About 90% of images contain one target and the published target-number plot starts at one. No dedicated target-free population is documented; background pixels provide negatives within selected images.
partition_evidence: The original paper uses approximately 50% train, 20% validation and 30% test. Later papers vary, so their splits cannot be silently equated with the original protocol.
quality_control: Motion confirmation supplies a documented target-selection check. No mask-boundary adjudication or inter-annotator agreement was verified, and the one-image-per-source rule was not independently checked against a manifest.
evaluation_meaning: nIoU averages image-level overlaps. Fixed-threshold mask scores and a receiver-operating-characteristic curve across thresholds answer different evaluation questions; neither establishes fine-grained object identity or event semantics.
independence_limits: Selecting one representative image per sequence is intended to avoid sequence overlap. It does not independently prove different acquisition sites, underlying targets or source-video lineage without source metadata.
new_findings: Motion in the source video confirms target reality before single-frame selection.
Five annotation forms in the paper exceed the two explicitly confirmed in current release documentation.
Authors request the name SIRST rather than NUAA-SIRST.
interpretation: This is a generic infrared small-target resource with temporally informed selection and single-frame evaluation. Binary masks do not identify military objects.
unresolved: Availability of the other paper-described annotation forms; complete source manifest; dedicated negative population; boundary consistency and exact original split files.

name: CAMO
review_basis: Full original CAMO paper (CVIU 2019, later arXiv posting) and creator documentation. Images and segmentation masks were not independently audited.
sample_unit: The paper distinguishes CAMO: 1,250 camouflage-positive images, from CAMO-COCO: those 1,250 plus 1,250 COCO negatives, totalling 2,500. The earlier catalogue used the combined count under CAMO.
collection_method: About 3,000 web-search candidates were reduced to 1,250 by manually removing duplicates and low-resolution images. Content includes natural animal camouflage and artificial human camouflage.
label_generation: Three people independently marked each positive image using an interactive segmentation tool. Masks represent camouflaged foreground; they are not fine-grained object identities. The paper reports 2–5 minutes per annotator/image.
negative_policy: The COCO comparison half has all-zero camouflage masks even when ordinary objects are visible. Negative therefore means no camouflaged foreground, not no object.
partition_evidence: Each positive/negative half is randomly split 1,000 train / 250 test. Source-site or source-photo grouping across these splits is not established.
quality_control: Multiple independent annotators and documented filtering provide process evidence. Their agreement, reconciliation procedure and residual pixel error are not quantified in the inspected sections.
evaluation_meaning: CAMO-only segmentation assumes camouflage is present; CAMO-COCO also examines responses when it is absent. These evaluation populations should not be conflated.
independence_limits: COCO reuse creates a known dependency on an existing collection. Natural and artificial camouflage categories do not establish a general military identity taxonomy. CAMO++ is a separate extension.
new_findings: Corrected the naming distinction between 1,250-image CAMO and 2,500-image CAMO-COCO.
Verified zero masks for non-camouflaged COCO images and three independent annotators.
interpretation: The key scientific distinction is camouflage foreground versus ordinary visible objects. Its negative policy makes that distinction explicit.

name: LEVIR-CC
review_basis: Read the recovered 20-page original paper, especially section III, and creator repository documentation. Caption JSON, imagery and archive contents were not independently audited.
sample_unit: 10,077 before/after image pairs and 50,385 caption records, five per pair. Published counts separate 5,038 changed and 5,039 no-change pairs; multiple captions are not independent visual observations.
collection_method: The paper says imagery mainly derives from LEVIR-CD: 20 Texas regions, 0.5 m/pixel and 5–15-year intervals. Original 1024×1024 pairs are cropped to 256×256. Pixel registration is an author claim, not an independently measured error bound.
label_generation: Five different annotators provide descriptions per pair. Instructions emphasize significant object changes and appearing/disappearing objects while excluding irrelevant appearance differences. No-change pairs use five prescribed sentences; these are standardized references, not unrestricted independent descriptions. LEVIR-MCI masks are a separate release product.
negative_policy: No-change means only irrelevant changes under the annotation policy. Examples ignore lighting, shadows and small tree-related changes; it does not mean pixel identity or absence of all real-world activity.
partition_evidence: Table I gives 6,815 training, 1,333 validation and 1,929 test pairs. Changed/no-change counts are 3,407/3,408, 667/666 and 964/965 respectively. These nearly balanced assignments do not establish source-image or regional separation.
quality_control: Authors checked spelling and grammar. Their human-agreement experiment scores one reference against four others using BLEU, METEOR and ROUGE-L. This measures linguistic agreement, not independent factual correctness or annotator consensus about every visible change.
evaluation_meaning: Reference-caption scores concern visible differences. The paper omits CIDEr-D for its no-change-only evaluation because repetitive vocabulary drives that metric near zero, illustrating how reference construction changes metric interpretation.
independence_limits: Derived subtiles can share parent imagery, and the collection primarily reuses LEVIR-CD. Five fixed no-change references and multiple descriptions per pair do not add independent scenes.
new_findings: Recovered exact partitions, near-equal changed/no-change sampling and prescribed no-change language.
Separated the paper's reference-agreement measurement from factual annotation validation.
interpretation: The primary paper substantially strengthens the methodological record, while its label definition remains narrower than unrestricted change or event understanding.
unresolved: Manifest-level source-image and regional split independence.
Independent visual/factual caption audit and residual registration error.

name: LEVIR-CD (original release)
review_basis: Creator dataset page and original STANet repository documentation. Publisher full text returned HTTP 403; no image/mask archive was audited.
sample_unit: 637 original 1024×1024 image pairs at 0.5 m/pixel, with 31,333 changed-building instances according to the creator. Later 256×256 tiles are derivatives of these original pairs.
collection_method: Google Earth imagery covers 20 regions in Texas, with acquisition years 2002–2018 and paired intervals of 5–14 years. Seasonal and illumination differences are intentionally present.
label_generation: Experts mark binary building-related change: new construction or decline. Every sample is labelled by one interpreter and checked by another according to the creator.
negative_policy: Zero denotes no annotated building change. It does not mean no other change, no building, or no activity. Seasonal appearance differences are meant to remain negative for this particular label definition.
partition_evidence: Official train/validation/test folder structure is documented. STANet describes non-overlapping 256×256 crops. Geographic independence of all partitions was not established by an inspected spatial audit.
quality_control: Two-person review gives process evidence but no measured residual error or boundary agreement. The creator added per-sample geographic information in 2023, making source-location relationships more inspectable.
evaluation_meaning: Masks measure visible building change between two dates. They neither date an intervening event precisely nor explain the cause of disappearance or construction.
independence_limits: Spatially adjacent chips and all subtiles of an original image share context. The original LEVIR-CD and the later LEVIR-CD+ extension are different releases.
new_findings: Confirmed the exact meaning of zero labels and the original-to-subtile relationship.
Creator documentation records a 2023 geographic-metadata supplement, not a new independent image collection.
interpretation: This is a well-bounded building-change task with a documented review process, but restricted geography and broad time gaps limit interpretation beyond that label definition.
unresolved: Spatial split audit using the geographic supplement.

name: RSICD
review_basis: Creator documentation plus direct parsing of the public annotation JSON; exact filename/string comparisons only. No image pixels or caption correctness were audited.
sample_unit: Verified 10,921 image records with 10,921 distinct filenames and 54,605 sentence records, exactly five per image. Five records do not imply five distinct texts.
collection_method: Creator documentation lists Google Earth, Baidu Map, MapABC and Tianditu imagery, standardized to 224×224 with varying original resolution. A complete original-source/location manifest is not established.
label_generation: The JSON associates raw sentences and tokens with image identifiers and split fields. The inspected metadata establishes associations, not whether sentences are complete or visually correct.
negative_policy: This is not a foreground/background detector benchmark. Captions can omit visible objects; omission from a sentence is not evidence of absence.
partition_evidence: Directly counted 8,734 train, 1,094 validation and 1,093 test image records. Unique filenames do not prove source-scene or pixel independence across those partitions.
quality_control: There are 18,190 globally distinct raw exact caption strings. Within-image comparisons trim outer whitespace: 10,197 images have repeated strings among their five captions; only 724 have five distinct captions.
evaluation_meaning: Text-reference metrics reflect this repeated reference structure. Repetition reduces reference diversity but does not alone establish incorrect captions or invalid benchmark results.
independence_limits: Image records can originate from shared maps or nearby locations, and repeated generic sentences can occur across unrelated scenes. The check did not measure visual duplication or semantic equivalence.
new_findings: Verified split/image/caption counts directly from creator JSON.
Per-image distinct-caption counts: 4,853 have one; 1,667 two; 2,182 three; 1,495 four; 724 five.
interpretation: The most substantial new evidence is a reproducible distinction between sentence-record count and reference-language diversity. It warrants precise wording about what five captions means.
unresolved: Reason for repeated caption records and any corrected release.
Independent visual/factual caption audit.

name: RSVQA-HR
review_basis: Full primary RSVQA paper v2 and creator repository; no complete image or QA archive independently audited.
sample_unit: 10,659 image patches and 1,066,316 question–answer pairs from 161 source tiles. Many questions reuse each patch.
collection_method: USGS aerial RGB orthophotos, 512×512 patches. The dataset subsection states 15 cm and a matching patch area; the conclusion instead says 30 cm, an internal discrepancy.
label_generation: OSM features and question templates generate presence, counting, comparison and area questions. Counts are exact answer categories; areas are quantized. Rural/urban questions belong to LR, not HR.
negative_policy: A no/zero answer means no matching mapped entity under the query definition. Missing OSM entries, misregistration or acquisition-date mismatch can produce an incorrect apparent negative.
partition_evidence: The paper separates source tiles and includes a second test set in Philadelphia with a sensor absent from training; the first test set covers similar regions to training. Manifest-level verification remains open.
quality_control: The paper openly discusses incomplete map annotations and date mismatch. Automatic generation is reproducible but is not an independent human verification of every image/answer pair.
evaluation_meaning: The original model still achieved 73.78% overall accuracy on test 1 and 72.51% on test 2 when images were randomly reassigned to questions. These author-reported controls show strong answer/language priors.
independence_limits: Questions from one patch are correlated, and template vocabulary is narrower than unrestricted conversation. Neither answer accuracy nor mapped relations establishes open-ended scenario comprehension.
new_findings: HR separates in-region and unseen-region/sensor tests; those test scores have different meanings.
The paper includes a random-image control, a stronger caution about language bias than headline QA accuracy alone.
interpretation: This is a constrained map-derived visual-question benchmark. Its clearest contribution is explicit question construction and split methodology, accompanied by unusually candid bias analysis.
unresolved: QA factual correctness after time alignment.

name: RSVQA-LR
review_basis: Full primary RSVQA paper v2 and creator repository; no complete image or QA archive independently audited.
sample_unit: 772 image patches and 77,232 question–answer pairs from nine source tiles. The QA total does not represent 77,232 independent visual scenes.
collection_method: Low-cloud Sentinel-2 RGB tiles over the Netherlands, at 10 m resolution, divided into 256×256 patches. Only nine source tiles underlie the patch collection.
label_generation: OSM and templates generate presence, comparison, counting and rural/urban questions. Count answers are binned; rural/urban is a building-density rule, not independent land-use adjudication.
negative_policy: A no/zero answer means no matching mapped entity under the query definition. Missing OSM entries, misregistration or acquisition-date mismatch can produce an incorrect apparent negative.
partition_evidence: Source tiles, rather than individual questions, are split 7 training / 1 validation / 1 test. This limits spatial leakage, though the small number of source tiles constrains geographic breadth.
quality_control: The paper openly discusses incomplete map annotations and date mismatch. Automatic generation is reproducible but is not an independent human verification of every image/answer pair.
evaluation_meaning: The original model retained 73.78% overall accuracy with randomly reassigned images, versus about 79.08% normally. This author-reported control shows that many correct answers need little image evidence.
independence_limits: Questions from one patch are correlated, and template vocabulary is narrower than unrestricted conversation. Neither answer accuracy nor mapped relations establishes open-ended scenario comprehension.
new_findings: LR rural/urban labels are rule-generated and its numerical answers are categories, not precise counts.
The paper includes a random-image control, a stronger caution about language bias than headline QA accuracy alone.
interpretation: This is a constrained map-derived visual-question benchmark. Its clearest contribution is explicit question construction and split methodology, accompanied by unusually candid bias analysis.

name: SARChat-2M / SARChat-Bench
review_basis: Full paper v5 and creator repository. The README dataset URL remained a YourOrg/SARChat placeholder at review; no released dialogue archive was verified.
sample_unit: 2,063,548 dialogue samples: 1,836,912 training and 226,636 test. They reuse SARDet-100K imagery and labels rather than introducing two million independently acquired images.
collection_method: SARDet-100K already combines multiple source datasets. SARChat adds six language task families over those inherited object annotations.
label_generation: Templates derive category, counts, box coordinates, image-relative positions and size/shape descriptions. Here cross-modal identification receives coordinates and describes attributes; it is not evidence of paired optical/SAR acquisitions.
negative_policy: Missing source boxes can propagate into incorrect counts or absent descriptions. The authors even show an example containing an additional object absent from original annotations; exhaustive scene truth is therefore not established.
partition_evidence: Train/test dialogue totals are reported. Complete source-image and constituent-dataset partition independence were not verified from a downloaded dialogue manifest.
quality_control: The fine-grained description subset filters small images, very small or unusually shaped boxes and invalid coordinates. These checks concern geometry and selection, not independent verification of category identity or caption truth.
evaluation_meaning: The benchmark evaluates structured tasks, including box overlap and attribute agreement. A geometry-derived description score is narrower evidence than an independently verified explanation of a scene.
independence_limits: Many tasks repeat each image. Roughly 77.5% of dialogue entries are cross-modal identification, so the overall two-million count is strongly influenced by one task’s generation scheme.
new_findings: Clarified the paper’s cross-modal identification term and strong task-count imbalance.
The public release remains unverified because the official dataset link is a placeholder; paper and code access are different.
interpretation: This is a large structured-text derivative whose core evidence comes from existing annotation geometry. Its scale and language form should not obscure inherited source limitations.
unresolved: Actual public dialogue archive and image-ID split audit.

name: xBD
review_basis: Full primary xBD paper, including annotation instructions and limitations; no image or polygon archive independently audited.
sample_unit: 22,068 pre/post images across 19 disasters; 850,736 polygon annotations. The damage-class counts sum to 425,368, consistent with pre/post representation, so 850,736 must not be called unique buildings.
collection_method: Disaster areas are selected to include damage and surrounding negative buffer. This deliberate selection is not an unbiased sample of all buildings or disaster damage prevalence.
label_generation: Pre-event building polygons are transferred to post-event imagery, then assigned ordinal damage levels. Post-event buildings without transferred pre-event polygons are deliberately ignored. Environmental factors use polygons in the detailed method, although the abstract calls them boxes.
negative_policy: No damage is a labelled category, but unannotated post-event structures are not certified negatives. Selection and transferred footprints determine which buildings enter assessment.
partition_evidence: Exact reported image counts are 18,336 train, 1,866 test and 1,866 holdout. The paper also says 80/10/10, which does not match those exact image counts; the discrepancy is retained.
quality_control: Multiple annotation rounds and expert review are described. Experts found and corrected 2–3% errors in a random sample, but no sample size or guarantee of the remaining error rate is provided.
evaluation_meaning: Damage classes are approximate interpretations from satellite imagery, explicitly distinguished by the authors from authoritative on-site structural inspection. They do not identify the cause of arbitrary damage.
independence_limits: Pre/post images share footprints and buildings; crops can share event context. Strong class imbalance favours no damage, and environmental visibility varies across disasters.
new_findings: Clarified the pre/post polygon counting unit and deliberately ignored unmatched post-event buildings.
Documented the qualified 2–3% correction statement, geometry wording conflict and split-percentage mismatch.
interpretation: This dataset supports a specific humanitarian observation: visible building damage after known disasters. Its annotation instructions are as consequential as its large headline scale.
unresolved: Complete release counts and explanation of split percentages.
